name: CUPID-Mo
summary: CUPID-Mo operated enriched lithium-molybdate scintillating bolometers at Modane. It validated the molybdenum-100 detector technology adopted for CUPID and produced a low-background double-beta-decay search.
detection_principle: Li2MoO4 crystals contain the isotope and measure decay energy as heat. Separate light detectors distinguish alpha particles from electron events, with coincidence cuts suppressing multisite backgrounds.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
